_comment: Shared redaction vectors. Two implementations must agree on these:
Every entry under `leaks` is a form the pre-2026-08 sanitizer passed
through verbatim into a signed receipt. The audit found the OpenClaw
plugin then auto-publishing that receipt, so these are not hypothetical.
`must_not_contain` is the real assertion -- checking for the presence of
[REDACTED] would pass on an implementation that redacts the wrong token.
`preserved` guards the opposite failure: a redactor that destroys the
whole command line hides the secret and the evidence together.

leaks.name: space-separated token flag
leaks.why: the exact case the old denylist missed: no `=`, so no pattern hit

leaks.name: short user:password pair
leaks.why: curl -u takes one positional argument containing both halves

leaks.name: URL userinfo password
leaks.why: the username is evidence and should survive; the password is not

leaks.name: stripe live key by prefix
leaks.why: no flag structure to lean on; only the vendor prefix identifies it

leaks.name: aws access key id by prefix
inline env assignment
leaks.why: the one thing the old sanitizer did catch; must not regress

benign.name: cargo build
benign.why: over-redaction destroys the evidence value of a receipt

benign.name: plain url
benign.why: a URL with no credentials must pass through untouched

benign.name: timestamp is not a user:password pair
flag with omitted value does not consume the next flag
benign.why: redacting --verbose here would corrupt the record and hide nothing
